dispositions.rationale: This is distinct from the extant Natural Proofs barrier and must retain the paper's algebraic-oracle model.
The fine-grained conjecture is not the Floyd-Warshall algorithm entry.
No existing CS record states both relativized oracle worlds.

The complexity catalog had no Blum-measure speedup theorem. The first Stage4 child left the speedup quantifiers implicit; exact_v1 freezes the Blum measure, total-computable speedup function and almost-everywhere comparison and supersedes that historical allocation.

Halting undecidability and recursion theorems do not state Busy Beaver domination. exact_v1 freezes Rado's n-state two-symbol blank-tape convention and uses S(n) for step activity rather than the symbol-productivity notation Sigma(n).
Computational and decisional Diffie-Hellman are different games and neither receives proof credit from ElGamal correctness.
ETH is absent and is an open hardness hypothesis rather than a proved lower bound.
GGM is distinct from Naor-Reingold and the generic PRF-existence row.
The result is an oracle and black-box barrier, not an unconditional impossibility theorem for cryptography.
Savitch and Immerman-Szelepcsenyi are related theorems but do not resolve L versus NL.
Search-LWE, decision-LWE, and SIS are distinct average-case problems; worst-to-average reductions are separate proved claims.
Existing classical and quantum complexity entries do not state this equality.
Nearby completeness and hierarchy rows do not represent this open equality question.
The fine-grained conjecture is absent and requires a frozen dimension and RAM convention.
THM-M-0720 / ATV-00000746 already denotes the exact P versus NP claim; record its missing computer-science catalog membership without creating a duplicate source occurrence or claim.
The umbrella phrase hides different loss, sample-complexity, and measurability contracts.
No present learning-theory branch states the shatter-function bound.
SETH is stronger than ETH and must have its own quantified k-SAT formulation.
The real-RAM and word-RAM variants must not be conflated; this fragment freezes the real-RAM variant.
Protocol-object rows do not supply the UC environment, adversary, session, and substitution theorem.
SyGuS is a problem schema and CEGIS is an architecture; it is a hard negative for the unrelated CEGAR row THM-C-0266.
THM-C-0231 is a broad Hoare-logic correctness occurrence; completeness and soundness are distinct exact children.
THM-C-0264 is a framework and THM-C-0265 an algorithm; neither alone states the fixpoint soundness theorem.
THM-C-0242 is an under-specified schema; a concrete compiler, semantics, undefined-behavior policy, and observation are required.
A memory model is an execution framework, not a theorem; the DRF guarantee is model-specific and truth-apt.
Party count, input partition, randomness, rounds, and error must be fixed before a communication claim is truth-apt.
The broad family lacks stream-update, pass, approximation, failure, and space conventions.
A property-testing claim requires an oracle model, distance measure, and error parameter.
Parameterized complexity is a framework; the parameter, reduction, and class must be explicit.
Average-case claims require a distribution ensemble, average-polynomial criterion, and reduction.
Online learning is not truth-apt without protocol, feedback, loss, and adversary semantics.
Relational expressiveness is a family; active-domain and safety conventions are needed for Codd's exact equivalence.
View, conflict, one-copy, and multiversion serializability are distinct notions.
Concurrency control is a method family; 2PL soundness has explicit lock-model hypotheses and no converse.

statement.natural_language: Under the algebraic-oracle definitions in Aaronson and Wigderson, the exhibited oracle and algebraic-extension counterworlds show that an algebrizing proof cannot resolve P versus NP.
hypotheses: Algebrizing and algebraic-oracle access are interpreted exactly as defined in the cited paper.
statement.conclusion: P versus NP requires a non-algebrizing ingredient relative to that proof-technique model.
statement.scope: Complexity-theoretic proof barrier; it does not assert that every technique using algebra is impossible.

material_status.basis: The primary paper proves the model-relative oracle barrier.

statement.natural_language: For every positive epsilon, exact all-pairs shortest paths on n-vertex directed graphs with O(log n)-bit integer edge weights has no O(n^(3-epsilon)) word-RAM algorithm.
hypotheses: Directed graph
Edge weights are O(log n)-bit integers
Standard word-RAM with word size Theta(log n)
Exact distances are required
statement.conclusion: No truly subcubic algorithm exists.
statement.scope: Deterministic standard fine-grained APSP variant; randomized and real-weight variants require separate records.

material_status.basis: The hypothesis remains an unresolved fine-grained assumption in the audited scope.

statement.natural_language: There are oracles A and B for which P^A equals NP^A while P^B does not equal NP^B.
hypotheses: P and NP are relativized to the same oracle in each world.
statement.conclusion: Both equality and separation occur under relativization.
statement.scope: Deterministic and nondeterministic polynomial-time oracle Turing machines.

material_status.basis: The two oracle constructions are proved in the primary paper.

statement.natural_language: For every admissible total recursive speedup function in a fixed Blum complexity measure, there is a total recursive function for which every program has another program computing the same function with the prescribed eventual speedup.
hypotheses: A Blum complexity measure is fixed
The requested speedup function satisfies the recursion and monotonicity conditions of the cited theorem
statement.conclusion: A total recursive function with no asymptotically optimal program under that prescribed speedup exists.
statement.scope: Quantifiers and eventual comparison follow the primary theorem; this is not a claim that every computable function admits arbitrary speedup.

material_status.basis: The machine-independent speedup theorem is proved in the primary paper.

additions.preferred_label: Busy Beaver domination and noncomputability theorem

statement.natural_language: For the fixed n-state Turing-machine convention, the Busy Beaver step function is not computable and eventually dominates every total computable numerical function after the fixed encoding overhead.
hypotheses: The Turing-machine alphabet, state counting, blank input, and halting convention are fixed
statement.conclusion: The Busy Beaver function is noncomputable and grows faster eventually than every total computable function.
statement.scope: Step-count Busy Beaver Sigma; symbol-count variants are separate but computably related.

material_status.basis: Rado proves noncomputability and the domination construction for the fixed machine model.

additions.preferred_label: Blum speedup theorem — exact almost-everywhere form

statement.natural_language: For every Blum complexity measure (phi,Phi) and every total computable two-argument speedup function r, there is a total computable predicate g such that every index i computing g has another index j computing g with r(x,Phi_j(x)) at most Phi_i(x) for all but finitely many x.
hypotheses: (phi_i) is a fixed effective numbering of the partial computable unary functions
Phi is a Blum complexity measure for that numbering: Phi_i(x) is defined exactly when phi_i(x) is defined, and the predicate Phi_i(x)=m is decidable in (i,x,m)
r:N x N -> N is total computable
statement.conclusion: There exists a total computable predicate g:N->{0,1} such that, for every i with phi_i=g, there exists j with phi_j=g and r(x,Phi_j(x))<=Phi_i(x) for all but finitely many x.
statement.scope: The almost-everywhere comparison means all natural-number inputs except a finite set. The theorem asserts existence of a speedup-bearing predicate for each r; it does not say that every computable function lacks an optimal program.

material_status.basis: Blum's primary JACM paper proves the machine-independent speedup theorem; the cited abstract-complexity reference exposes the quantified almost-everywhere form used here.

additions.preferred_label: Rado step Busy Beaver S(n) domination theorem — exact convention

statement.natural_language: Under Rado's n-state, two-symbol, blank-tape convention, the maximum halting step count S(n) is noncomputable and eventually exceeds every total computable numerical function.
hypotheses: n>=1; a machine has n nonhalting working states plus one distinguished halt state, one bi-infinite tape, symbols {0,1}, blank symbol 0, and starts in the first working state on an all-0 tape
For each working-state/symbol pair the deterministic transition writes 0 or 1, moves one cell left or right, and enters a working state or the halt state
S(n) is the maximum number of executed transitions before first entering the halt state among all such n-state machines that halt
statement.conclusion: S is not computable, and for every total computable f:N->N there exists N such that S(n)>f(n) for every n>=N.
statement.scope: This is Rado's step/activity function S(n). The productivity function Sigma(n), which maximizes the number of printed 1 symbols, is a separate variant.

material_status.basis: Rado's primary paper fixes the two-symbol blank-tape model and proves the noncomputability and domination behavior of the Busy Beaver functions.

statement.natural_language: For the fixed security-parameter-indexed cyclic-group generator, no probabilistic polynomial-time adversary given (g, g^a, g^b) outputs g^(ab) with non-negligible probability over uniform exponents and group generation.
hypotheses: A polynomial-time cyclic-group generator is fixed
Exponents a and b are uniform
Adversaries are uniform probabilistic polynomial time
statement.conclusion: Computing the Diffie-Hellman shared group element has only negligible success probability.
statement.scope: The named group family and uniform-adversary convention; nonuniform and gap variants are separate.

material_status.basis: CDH is retained as an unproved hardness assumption, not as a theorem.

statement.natural_language: For the fixed security-parameter-indexed cyclic-group generator, no probabilistic polynomial-time adversary distinguishes (g,g^a,g^b,g^(ab)) from (g,g^a,g^b,g^c) with non-negligible advantage for uniform a,b,c.
hypotheses: A polynomial-time cyclic-group generator is fixed
Exponents a, b, and c are uniform
Adversaries are uniform probabilistic polynomial time
statement.conclusion: The Diffie-Hellman tuple and an independent random tuple are computationally indistinguishable.
statement.scope: The named group family; CDH, decisional linear, and pairing-friendly variants are distinct.

material_status.basis: DDH is retained as an unproved hardness assumption, not inferred from ElGamal correctness.

statement.natural_language: There is a constant c greater than zero such that 3-SAT on n variables cannot be decided in deterministic time 2^(c n) times a polynomial in the input length.
hypotheses: Standard binary encoding of 3-CNF formulas
Worst-case deterministic running time
statement.conclusion: 3-SAT has no subexponential-time algorithm in the number of variables.
statement.scope: Deterministic ETH; randomized ETH is a separate variant.

material_status.basis: ETH remains an explicit unresolved hardness hypothesis in the audited scope.

statement.natural_language: If G is a secure length-doubling pseudorandom generator with halves G0 and G1, then the keyed binary-tree family F_s(x_1...x_n)=G_(x_n)(...G_(x_1)(s)) is a pseudorandom function family against probabilistic polynomial-time oracle distinguishers.
hypotheses: G is a length-doubling PRG secure for the fixed uniform PPT convention
Inputs have the fixed polynomial length n
The oracle distinguisher has polynomial query and time bounds
statement.conclusion: The GGM tree construction is a secure PRF with the hybrid loss proved in the source.
statement.scope: Classical uniform computational security; this is distinct from Naor-Reingold.

material_status.basis: The reduction is proved assuming the stated PRG security premise.

statement.natural_language: In the oracle and black-box-reduction model of Impagliazzo and Rudich, there is an oracle world with one-way permutations but without secure key agreement, ruling out a relativizing black-box implication of key agreement from one-way permutations.
hypotheses: Security and construction access are relativized exactly as in the cited model
statement.conclusion: No proof of the specified black-box relativizing form establishes key agreement from one-way permutations.
statement.scope: Model-relative barrier; it is not an unconditional separation between symmetric and public-key cryptography.

material_status.basis: The primary paper proves the oracle separation.

statement.natural_language: Does deterministic logarithmic space equal nondeterministic logarithmic space?
hypotheses: Read-only input and O(log n) work tape under the standard language-decision model
statement.conclusion: L = NL.
statement.scope: Classical uniform language classes under logspace reductions.

material_status.basis: The current complexity-class reference continues to list the equality as unresolved.

statement.natural_language: For the fixed functions n(lambda), q(lambda), sample count, and error distribution chi, no probabilistic polynomial-time algorithm recovers uniform secret s from polynomially many samples (a, <a,s>+e mod q) with non-negligible probability.
hypotheses: a is uniform in Z_q^n
s is uniform in Z_q^n
e is sampled independently from chi
All parameters are security-parameter indexed
statement.conclusion: The secret cannot be recovered with non-negligible probability by uniform PPT algorithms.
statement.scope: Search-LWE for the frozen parameter family; decision-LWE is a separate record.

material_status.basis: This is an explicit average-case hardness assumption; worst-case reductions do not prove the assumption unconditionally.

statement.natural_language: For the fixed functions n(lambda), q(lambda), sample count, and error distribution chi, no probabilistic polynomial-time distinguisher has non-negligible advantage between LWE samples (a,<a,s>+e mod q) and uniform samples in Z_q^n x Z_q.
hypotheses: a and s are uniform
e is sampled independently from chi
All parameters are security-parameter indexed
statement.conclusion: LWE samples and uniform samples are computationally indistinguishable.
statement.scope: Decision-LWE for the frozen parameter family; search-decision equivalences require separate parameterized reductions.

material_status.basis: This is an explicit hardness assumption and is not upgraded by the existence of conditional reductions.

statement.natural_language: For uniform A in Z_q^(n by m) and the frozen parameter functions, no probabilistic polynomial-time algorithm finds a nonzero integer vector z with A z = 0 modulo q and norm at most beta with non-negligible probability.
hypotheses: A is uniform
m, n, q, beta and the chosen norm satisfy the frozen parameter regime
Algorithms are uniform PPT
statement.conclusion: A short nonzero modular-kernel vector is average-case hard to find.
statement.scope: The specified SIS norm and parameters; Ajtai's worst-to-average theorem is a separate proved claim.

material_status.basis: This is an explicit average-case hardness assumption; the cited reduction supplies conditional support, not an unconditional proof.

statement.natural_language: In the explicit AT-S4-CGP1 prime-order group ensemble, the probability that any uniform probabilistic polynomial-time adversary given (1^lambda,p_lambda,q_lambda,g_lambda,g_lambda^a,g_lambda^b) outputs g_lambda^(ab) is negligible in lambda.
hypotheses: lambda ranges over integers at least 16; q_lambda is the least prime not smaller than 2^lambda; p_lambda is the least prime congruent to 1 modulo q_lambda

h_lambda is the least integer h at least 2 with h^((p_lambda-1)/q_lambda) not congruent to 1 modulo p_lambda; g_lambda=h_lambda^((p_lambda-1)/q_lambda) modulo p_lambda; G_lambda=<g_lambda> is represented by canonical residues modulo p_lambda and has prime order q_lambda
The public nonuniform parameter sequence (p_lambda,q_lambda,g_lambda) is supplied to the adversary; a and b are sampled independently and uniformly from Z_(q_lambda)
The adversary is one uniform probabilistic polynomial-time Turing machine measured in lambda; success probability is over a,b and its internal coins; negligible has its standard asymptotic meaning
statement.conclusion: Pr[A(1^lambda,p_lambda,q_lambda,g_lambda,g_lambda^a,g_lambda^b)=g_lambda^(ab)] is negligible in lambda.
statement.scope: Exact parameter profile AT-S4-CGP1. The public parameters form a mathematically fixed nonuniform sequence; no efficient parameter-generation claim is made. Other finite-field, elliptic-curve, generic-group, nonuniform-adversary, and gap-CDH profiles are separate variants.

material_status.basis: This exact security-parameter-indexed CDH game is retained as an unproved hardness assumption; the primary source motivates the computational Diffie-Hellman problem but does not prove its hardness.

statement.natural_language: In the explicit AT-S4-CGP1 prime-order group ensemble, every uniform probabilistic polynomial-time adversary has negligible distinguishing advantage between (g_lambda^a,g_lambda^b,g_lambda^(ab)) and (g_lambda^a,g_lambda^b,g_lambda^c).
hypotheses: lambda ranges over integers at least 16; q_lambda is the least prime not smaller than 2^lambda; p_lambda is the least prime congruent to 1 modulo q_lambda

h_lambda is the least integer h at least 2 with h^((p_lambda-1)/q_lambda) not congruent to 1 modulo p_lambda; g_lambda=h_lambda^((p_lambda-1)/q_lambda) modulo p_lambda; G_lambda=<g_lambda> is represented by canonical residues modulo p_lambda and has prime order q_lambda
The public nonuniform parameter sequence (p_lambda,q_lambda,g_lambda) is supplied to the adversary; a,b,c are sampled independently and uniformly from Z_(q_lambda)
The adversary is one uniform probabilistic polynomial-time Turing machine measured in lambda; advantage is the absolute difference of its output-one probabilities in the real and random games
statement.conclusion: |Pr[A(1^lambda,p_lambda,q_lambda,g_lambda,g_lambda^a,g_lambda^b,g_lambda^(ab))=1]-Pr[A(1^lambda,p_lambda,q_lambda,g_lambda,g_lambda^a,g_lambda^b,g_lambda^c)=1]| is negligible in lambda.
statement.scope: Exact parameter profile AT-S4-CGP1. The public parameters form a mathematically fixed nonuniform sequence; no efficient parameter-generation claim is made. CDH, pairing-friendly, decisional-linear, elliptic-curve, generic-group, and nonuniform-adversary variants are separate.

material_status.basis: This exact security-parameter-indexed DDH game is retained as an unproved hardness assumption and receives no proof credit from ElGamal correctness.

statement.natural_language: For the explicit AT-S4-LP1 parameter profile, no uniform probabilistic polynomial-time algorithm recovers the uniform secret from the m(lambda) Search-LWE samples with non-negligible probability.
hypotheses: lambda ranges over integers at least 16; n(lambda)=lambda; q(lambda) is the least prime not smaller than n(lambda)^3; m(lambda)=ceiling(2*n(lambda)*log_2(q(lambda)))

sigma(lambda)=2*sqrt(n(lambda))*(ln n(lambda))^2; chi_lambda is the discrete Gaussian on Z with probability proportional to exp(-pi*z^2/sigma(lambda)^2), independently sampled and then reduced modulo q(lambda)
The secret s is uniform in Z_q^n; for i=1,...,m, a_i is independently uniform in Z_q^n and e_i is independently sampled from chi_lambda; the input sample is (a_i,<a_i,s>+e_i mod q)
The adversary is one uniform probabilistic polynomial-time Turing machine measured in lambda; all integers and vectors use canonical binary encodings
statement.conclusion: Pr[A(1^lambda,(a_i,<a_i,s>+e_i mod q)_(i=1)^m)=s] is negligible in lambda.
statement.scope: Exact parameter profile AT-S4-LP1 with n=lambda, q the least prime at least n^3, m=ceiling(2n log_2 q), and the stated discrete-Gaussian error. Decision-LWE, other secret/error distributions, module/ring LWE, and worst-to-average reductions are separate.

material_status.basis: The game is now a closed asymptotic proposition for AT-S4-LP1, but its average-case hardness remains an assumption; Regev's reductions do not unconditionally prove it.

statement.natural_language: For the explicit AT-S4-LP1 parameter profile, every uniform probabilistic polynomial-time algorithm has negligible advantage in distinguishing m(lambda) LWE samples sharing one uniform secret from m(lambda) independent uniform pairs.
hypotheses: lambda ranges over integers at least 16; n(lambda)=lambda; q(lambda) is the least prime not smaller than n(lambda)^3; m(lambda)=ceiling(2*n(lambda)*log_2(q(lambda)))

sigma(lambda)=2*sqrt(n(lambda))*(ln n(lambda))^2; chi_lambda is the discrete Gaussian on Z with probability proportional to exp(-pi*z^2/sigma(lambda)^2), independently sampled and then reduced modulo q(lambda)

In the LWE game one secret s is uniform in Z_q^n and each pair is (a_i,<a_i,s>+e_i mod q) with independent uniform a_i and independent e_i from chi_lambda; in the uniform game all m pairs are independently uniform in Z_q^n x Z_q
The adversary is one uniform probabilistic polynomial-time Turing machine measured in lambda; advantage is the absolute output-one probability difference and all encodings are canonical binary
statement.conclusion: The distinguishing advantage between the AT-S4-LP1 LWE and uniform games is negligible in lambda.
statement.scope: Exact parameter profile AT-S4-LP1. Search-decision reductions, alternative secrets/errors, module/ring LWE, and nonuniform distinguishers are separate.

material_status.basis: The two distributions and every parameter are frozen, but their computational indistinguishability remains an unproved hardness assumption.

additions.preferred_label: Short Integer Solution assumption — AT-S4-LP1 profile

statement.natural_language: For the explicit AT-S4-LP1 parameter profile, no uniform probabilistic polynomial-time algorithm given uniform A in Z_q^(n by m) finds a nonzero integer vector z with A z=0 modulo q and Euclidean norm at most beta(lambda) with non-negligible probability.
hypotheses: lambda ranges over integers at least 16; n(lambda)=lambda; q(lambda) is the least prime not smaller than n(lambda)^3; m(lambda)=ceiling(2*n(lambda)*log_2(q(lambda)))
beta(lambda)=ceiling(n(lambda)*sqrt(m(lambda))); A is sampled uniformly from Z_(q(lambda))^(n(lambda) by m(lambda))
A solution is z in Z^m minus {0} with A z congruent to zero modulo q and Euclidean norm ||z||_2 at most beta(lambda)
The adversary is one uniform probabilistic polynomial-time Turing machine measured in lambda; A and z use canonical binary encodings
statement.conclusion: Pr[A_sis(1^lambda,A) outputs a valid nonzero z with ||z||_2<=beta(lambda)] is negligible in lambda.
statement.scope: Exact parameter profile AT-S4-LP1 with the Euclidean norm. Infinity-norm SIS, other dimensions/moduli/bounds, module/ring SIS, and Ajtai's worst-to-average reduction theorem are separate.

material_status.basis: The random-instance distribution and solution relation are frozen, but average-case hardness for this profile remains an assumption rather than a consequence of the cited reduction alone.

aliases: Entangled multiprover interactive proofs equal recursively enumerable languages

statement.natural_language: The class of languages with multiprover interactive proofs whose provers may share entanglement equals the class of recursively enumerable languages.
hypotheses: Completeness, soundness, verifier, and entangled-strategy conventions are those fixed in the primary paper
statement.conclusion: MIP* = RE.
statement.scope: Classical polynomial-time verifier with noncommunicating entangled provers.

material_status.basis: The equality is the main theorem of the primary source.

statement.natural_language: Does nondeterministic polynomial time equal its complement class?
hypotheses: Classical uniform language-decision model with polynomial-time many-one encodings
statement.conclusion: NP = coNP.
statement.scope: Equivalent standard formulation: TAUT belongs to NP.

material_status.basis: The current complexity reference continues to treat the equality as unresolved.

statement.natural_language: For every positive epsilon there is a constant c such that deciding whether n Boolean vectors in dimension d=c log n contain an orthogonal pair has no O(n^(2-epsilon)) word-RAM algorithm.
hypotheses: Boolean vectors
Dimension d=c log n
Word size Theta(log n)
Worst-case deterministic time
statement.conclusion: No truly subquadratic algorithm solves Orthogonal Vectors in this regime.
statement.scope: Standard deterministic OVC; randomized variants require a separate record.

material_status.basis: OVC remains an unresolved fine-grained hardness assumption in the audited scope.

additions.preferred_label: Realizable PAC learnability and finite VC dimension equivalence
aliases: Fundamental theorem of realizable PAC learning

statement.natural_language: Under the standard measurability conditions, a binary concept class is distribution-free PAC learnable in the realizable case if and only if it has finite VC dimension.
hypotheses: Binary classification
IID examples
Realizable labels
Distribution-free PAC criterion
The standard measurability assumptions
statement.conclusion: PAC learnability is equivalent to finite VC dimension.
statement.scope: Realizable PAC learning; agnostic learning and exact sample bounds are separate variants.

material_status.basis: The learnability characterization is proved in the primary source.

additions.preferred_label: Agnostic PAC learnability and finite VC dimension equivalence
aliases: Fundamental theorem of agnostic binary learning

statement.natural_language: Under the standard measurability conditions and zero-one loss, a binary hypothesis class is distribution-free agnostically PAC learnable if and only if it has finite VC dimension.
hypotheses: Binary hypotheses
IID labeled examples with arbitrary label noise
Zero-one loss
Distribution-free agnostic PAC criterion
The standard measurability assumptions
statement.conclusion: Agnostic PAC learnability is equivalent to finite VC dimension.
statement.scope: Agnostic binary classification; regression and other losses are separate.

material_status.basis: Kearns, Schapire, and Sellie supply the primary agnostic-learning model, and the cited statistical-learning reference states the finite-VC-dimension characterization for the separately scoped agnostic binary model.

statement.natural_language: If a family F of subsets of an n-element set has VC dimension d, then |F| is at most the sum from i=0 through d of binomial(n,i).
hypotheses: F is a family of subsets of a finite n-element ground set
VCdim(F)=d
statement.conclusion: |F| <= sum_{i=0}^d binomial(n,i).
statement.scope: Finite set systems.

material_status.basis: The combinatorial bound is proved independently in the cited primary sources.

statement.natural_language: For every positive epsilon there exists k such that k-SAT on n variables has no deterministic O((2-epsilon)^n poly(n)) algorithm.
hypotheses: Standard binary encoding of k-CNF
Worst-case deterministic running time
k may depend on epsilon
statement.conclusion: No single base below 2 gives exponential-time algorithms for all k-SAT widths.
statement.scope: Deterministic SETH; randomized SETH is separate.

material_status.basis: SETH remains an unresolved hardness hypothesis in the audited scope.

statement.natural_language: For every positive epsilon, deciding whether n real inputs contain three distinct indexed elements whose sum is zero has no O(n^(2-epsilon)) real-RAM algorithm.
hypotheses: Standard unit-cost real-RAM
Exact arithmetic and comparison operations
Three distinct input indices
statement.conclusion: No truly subquadratic algorithm solves this 3SUM variant.
statement.scope: Real-RAM 3SUM; bounded-integer word-RAM variants are separate.

material_status.basis: The standard truly-subquadratic conjecture remains unresolved in the frozen real-RAM scope.

statement.natural_language: If protocol rho UC-emulates ideal functionality F and protocol pi UC-realizes G in the F-hybrid model, then the protocol obtained by replacing each F call in pi by rho UC-emulates G.
hypotheses: The environment, adversary, corruption, scheduling, and session conventions are fixed to the cited UC model
rho UC-emulates F
pi UC-realizes G in the F-hybrid model
statement.conclusion: The composed protocol pi^rho UC-emulates G.
statement.scope: The universal-composability model and admissibility conditions of the primary source.

material_status.basis: The composition implication is proved under the explicit UC premises.

statement.natural_language: For a finite SyGuS candidate language, a fair no-repeat CEGIS loop using a sound and complete verifier terminates with a satisfying candidate if one exists and otherwise terminates after exhausting all candidates.
hypotheses: The grammar denotes a finite candidate set
Candidate enumeration is fair and never repeats
The verifier is sound and complete and returns a genuine counterexample for each incorrect candidate
statement.conclusion: CEGIS terminates and is complete for the finite candidate set.
statement.scope: Finite candidate languages only; no completeness claim is made for infinite grammars or incomplete solvers.

material_status.basis: The result follows by finite exhaustion under the explicit SyGuS/CEGIS contract.

additions.preferred_label: Cook relative completeness of Hoare logic

statement.natural_language: For the specified while language and interpretation I, if the assertion language is expressive for the required strongest postconditions, every semantically valid partial-correctness triple is derivable from Hoare rules together with all true assertions of I.
hypotheses: The imperative language and operational interpretation I are those of the cited theorem
Partial correctness is intended
The assertion language satisfies Cook expressiveness
All true formulas of the underlying interpretation are available as an oracle theory
statement.conclusion: Semantic validity of a Hoare triple implies derivability relative to the assertion theory.
statement.scope: Relative, not effective absolute, completeness of partial-correctness Hoare logic.

material_status.basis: Cook's theorem and corrigendum prove the stated relative-completeness result.

aliases: Galois-connection soundness theorem for abstract interpretation

statement.natural_language: Let C and A be complete lattices with abstraction and concretization alpha left adjoint to gamma. If monotone F and F-sharp satisfy F composed with gamma <= gamma composed with F-sharp, then every abstract post-fixpoint a with F-sharp(a)<=a safely over-approximates the least concrete fixpoint: lfp(F)<=gamma(a).
hypotheses: C and A are complete lattices
alpha is left adjoint to gamma
F and F-sharp are monotone
F(gamma(a)) <= gamma(F-sharp(a))
a is an abstract post-fixpoint
statement.conclusion: lfp(F) <= gamma(a).
statement.scope: Order-theoretic abstract interpretation; widening termination is a separate claim.

material_status.basis: The lattice and fixpoint soundness construction is proved in the foundational paper.

statement.natural_language: For a source program accepted and compiled by the CompCert version described in the primary paper, under its source and target semantics and defined-behavior precondition, every observable behavior of the generated target program is permitted by the source program.
hypotheses: The compiler, passes, source language, target language, and semantics are fixed to the cited CompCert artifact
Compilation succeeds
The source program satisfies the theorem's defined-behavior and safety preconditions
statement.conclusion: Target behaviors refine the allowed source behaviors under the paper's observation relation.
statement.scope: The cited CompCert release and semantics; later releases and stronger backward-simulation claims need separate evidence.

material_status.basis: The concrete semantic-preservation theorem is machine-checked and reported in the primary paper under its stated preconditions.

statement.natural_language: In the cited C++ concurrency model, a program whose relevant executions are data-race-free under the model's synchronization discipline receives the model's sequential-consistency guarantee for those executions.
hypotheses: Events, reads-from, modification order, happens-before, and data race are those of the pinned C++ model
The program satisfies the model's data-race-free premise
Only the covered atomic and non-atomic operations are used
statement.conclusion: Allowed observable behavior is represented by an execution consistent with the guaranteed sequentially consistent semantics.
statement.scope: The cited C++ model; Java, C11 revisions, relaxed atomics, and out-of-thin-air variants are separate.

material_status.basis: The DRF guarantee is model-specific and proved under the synchronization premise.

statement.natural_language: For every total Boolean two-party function f, deterministic communication complexity D(f) is at least log base two of the real rank of its communication matrix M_f.
hypotheses: Two-party deterministic protocol
Total Boolean function
Worst-case exact computation
Communication matrix rank is over the real numbers
statement.conclusion: D(f) >= log_2 rank_R(M_f).
statement.scope: Deterministic exact two-party communication; randomized, quantum, and partial-function variants are separate.

material_status.basis: A c-bit deterministic protocol partitions the matrix into at most 2^c monochromatic rectangles, giving the rank bound.

statement.natural_language: In the one-pass turnstile stream model, the AMS sketch returns a (1 plus or minus epsilon) approximation to F2 with probability at least 1-delta using O(epsilon^-2 log(1/delta)) signed counters plus their logarithmic-bit seeds and storage.
hypotheses: One-pass turnstile updates over a fixed universe
Frequencies and stream length have the stated bit bounds
The sketch uses the required limited-independence random signs
epsilon and delta are in their standard ranges
statement.conclusion: The estimate lies in [(1-epsilon)F2,(1+epsilon)F2] with probability at least 1-delta.
statement.scope: Second frequency moment; insertion-only, sliding-window, and higher-moment bounds are separate.

material_status.basis: The primary paper proves the estimator moment bounds and amplification.

statement.natural_language: For oracle f from F_2^n to F_2, if the BLR check f(x)+f(y)=f(x+y) accepts with probability at least 1-epsilon for uniform independent x,y, then f is epsilon-close, under uniform Hamming distance, to a linear function; linear functions are always accepted.
hypotheses: Uniform independent oracle queries x and y
Arithmetic over F_2
Distance is uniform relative Hamming distance
epsilon is in the theorem's valid range
statement.conclusion: High BLR acceptance implies proximity to a linear function, yielding a one-sided O(1/epsilon)-query tester after repetition.
statement.scope: Boolean linearity testing; low-degree and other property tests are separate.

material_status.basis: The primary source proves completeness and quantitative soundness of the self-test.

statement.natural_language: The parameterized problem that asks whether a graph contains a clique of size k, parameterized by k, is complete for W[1] under fixed-parameter tractable many-one reductions.
hypotheses: Input is a finite simple graph and integer k
Parameter is k
Reductions are standard fpt many-one reductions
statement.conclusion: Parameterized k-Clique is W[1]-complete.
statement.scope: Classical parameterized decision complexity.

material_status.basis: The membership and hardness reductions are standard results documented in the cited reference.

additions.preferred_label: Existence of a DistNP-complete distributional problem

statement.natural_language: Under Levin's distributional-NP definitions and average-case reductions, there exists a distributional problem complete for DistNP.
hypotheses: Distribution ensembles and polynomial-time samplability/dominance are those in the cited framework
Reductions preserve average-case tractability in Levin's sense
statement.conclusion: DistNP has a complete distributional problem.
statement.scope: Levin's average-case model; modern alternative reduction notions require separate variants.

material_status.basis: The completeness construction is proved in the primary source.

statement.natural_language: For N binary experts, Weighted Majority with penalty beta in (0,1) makes at most [ln(1/beta)/ln(2/(1+beta))] times the mistakes of any fixed expert plus ln(N)/ln(2/(1+beta)) mistakes.
hypotheses: Binary outcomes and expert predictions
Initial expert weights are equal
After each error an expert's weight is multiplied by beta
The algorithm predicts by current weighted majority
statement.conclusion: For every expert i, M <= (ln(1/beta)/ln(2/(1+beta))) m_i + ln(N)/ln(2/(1+beta)).
statement.scope: Full-information mistake-bound protocol; Hedge losses and bandit feedback are separate.

material_status.basis: The multiplicative-weights potential argument is proved in the primary paper.

statement.natural_language: Over finite relational instances and under the fixed safety and active-domain convention, relational algebra and safe domain-independent relational calculus express the same queries.
hypotheses: Finite relational instances
Queries are safe or domain-independent under the stated active-domain semantics
Classical set semantics without aggregates, recursion, or nulls
statement.conclusion: Every relational-algebra query has an equivalent safe calculus query and conversely.
statement.scope: Classical first-order relational query languages; bags, SQL nulls, aggregation, and recursion are excluded.

material_status.basis: Codd's relational-completeness result supplies both translations in the scoped model.

statement.natural_language: A finite single-version read-write schedule is conflict-serializable if and only if its precedence graph is acyclic; every topological ordering of that graph gives a conflict-equivalent serial schedule.
hypotheses: Finite schedule
Single-version read-write transactions
Conflict equivalence uses the standard same-item read/write and write/write conflicts
statement.conclusion: Conflict serializability is equivalent to acyclicity of the precedence graph.
statement.scope: Conflict serializability only; view and multiversion serializability are separate.

material_status.basis: The graph characterization follows from the serializability theory in the primary source.

statement.natural_language: Every schedule generated by well-formed transactions obeying two-phase locking is conflict-serializable.
hypotheses: Each conflicting read or write is protected by the required lock
Transactions are well formed
Each transaction has a growing lock-acquisition phase followed by a shrinking release phase with no later acquisition
The standard single-version lock model is used
statement.conclusion: The resulting schedule is conflict-serializable.
statement.scope: Soundness of basic 2PL; strictness, recoverability, deadlock, multiversion protocols, and the false converse are excluded.

material_status.basis: The locking theorem is proved under the explicit well-formedness and two-phase premises.

additions.preferred_label: One-way functions imply P does not equal NP

statement.natural_language: If a length-regular polynomial-time computable one-way function exists against the fixed probabilistic polynomial-time inversion model, then P does not equal NP.
hypotheses: A standard length-regular uniform one-way function exists
Inversion success is measured over the function's prescribed efficiently samplable input distribution
Adversaries are uniform PPT
statement.conclusion: P != NP.
statement.scope: Uniform classical worst-case classes and average-case inversion security under the fixed OWF definition.

material_status.basis: If P equaled NP, the associated polynomially balanced inversion relation could be solved sufficiently to contradict one-wayness.

additions.preferred_label: P not equal to NP implies one-way functions

statement.natural_language: If P does not equal NP, then a length-regular polynomial-time computable one-way function exists against the fixed uniform probabilistic polynomial-time inversion model.
hypotheses: P != NP in the classical uniform language model
One-wayness uses the fixed efficiently samplable input distribution and negligible-inversion definition
statement.conclusion: A one-way function exists.
statement.scope: The worst-case-to-average-case converse; stronger average-case assumptions and nonuniform variants are separate.

material_status.basis: The converse from worst-case P != NP to average-case one-wayness remains open; the legacy source incorrectly presented it as established.

overlays.rationale: The exact P versus NP claim already exists as ATV-00000746; this overlay records its missing computer-science catalog membership without allocating or rebinding a claim.
The current source says P != NP implies one-way functions. The OWF-to-separation direction is proved, while this converse is open; neither child inherits evidence from the legacy prose.
